newsitem.title: CHINA: China says no change yet planned on H-share taxes.
newsitem.headline: China says no change yet planned on H-share taxes.

text.p: The Chinese government has no plans at present to change the preferential tax rate for 1998 applied to Chinese H-share firms listed in Hong Kong, a tax official said on Thursday.

The official with the State Administration of Taxation said any decision on next year's tax rates would be made by the State Council (cabinet) only after the economic outlook for this year became clearer.

"The State Council will study the whole year's general economic situation to decide next year's taxes," the official said. "So at present, no one can know whether the preferential treatment will be cancelled or not in 1998."
Nine H-share companies will continue to enjoy a preferential income tax rate of 15 percent in 1997, the Shanghai Securities News said on Tuesday.

The nine companies, the first batch of firms permitted to list in Hong Kong in 1993, include Shanghai Petrochemical, Tsingtao Brewery, Kunming Machine Tool and Beiren Printing Machinery, the newspaper said.
Maanshan Iron and Steel, Guangzhou Shipyard, Yizheng Chemical Fibre, Dongfang Electrical Machinery and Tianjin Bohai Chemical Industry are also on the list, it said.
China has 26 companies listed in Hong Kong. The other 17 H-share companies pay 33 percent income tax.
